metadata.datasource: Characteristic curves, spectral sensitivities, dye spectra from Kodak H-1-5293 (3-99), EASTMAN EXR 200T Color Negative Film 5293/7293, ECN-2, Status M. The curves were read from the vector plot, each layer by its order at the dense end, and converted from Status M densities into dye amounts. Mid-grey at the normal exposure, log H -1.301 lux-seconds: Kodak's 10/EI at EI 200 under tungsten, the rule the camera-stop scale on the sheet of its sister stock EXR 50D marks; this sheet draws no such scale. Past the sheet's last plotted exposure each curve continues at its final gradient for 0.8 decades (R 0.44, G 0.54, B 0.54), where the plot ends a few stops over normal and the film goes on. The sheet's sensitivity shapes continue on the donor's tails beyond the plotted range and are balanced so an 18% grey exposes every layer equally. The base density is the sheet's own D-min spectral density, base and fog, and the profile keeps its midscale neutral. The sheet plots no single-dye spectra: the dyes are those its sister stock's sheet plots ('kodak_exr_50d', of the same maker, generation and process), each moved and stretched about its peak until the three add up to this sheet's neutral over D-min: cyan +0.0 nm x1.000, magenta +0.0 nm x1.000, yellow +0.0 nm x1.000. No spectral adaptation window: agx fits one to each of its own stocks' sensitivities. DIR coupler model from 'kodak_vision3_200t'.
